title: Cybersecurity Warnings & Password Rules: Must & Must Not
workplace_track: Cybersecurity, Endpoint Protection & Zero Trust Architecture
description: Understand and communicate IT security policies, multi-factor authentication (MFA) guidelines, and credential safety rules using 'must', 'must not', and 'have to'.
learning_objectives: Use 'must' for mandatory security obligations and 'must not' for strict prohibitions
Differentiate 'must not' (prohibition: nesmět) from 'don't have to' (absence of obligation: nemuset)
Communicate cybersecurity policies clearly to end-users without modal confusion

questions.prompt: All corporate domain users _____ change their password every 90 days according to group policy.

explanations.correct: 'must' expresses mandatory corporate security policy obligations.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'musí změnit'. Obligatory corporate rules require 'must'.

questions.prompt: You _____ share your Active Directory credentials or MFA tokens with anyone, including IT support.

explanations.wrong_A: 'don't have to' means absence of necessity (nemusíte = you can if you want), which is a dangerous security flaw.

questions.cz_learning_point: Major Czenglish danger: 'must not' = nesmíte (zákaz). 'Don't have to' = nemusíte (není to nutné, ale můžete). Credential sharing is strictly 'must not'!

questions.prompt: Technicians _____ install unauthorized software on company-issued laptops.

explanations.correct: 'must not' is the negative modal expressing prohibition.
explanations.wrong_B: 'don't must' is completely ungrammatical in English.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'nesmí instalovat'. English prohibition is 'must not', never *don't must*.

questions.prompt: If you work from home, you _____ connect to the corporate VPN to access internal SharePoint sites.

explanations.correct: 'have to' expresses an external technical requirement/necessity.
explanations.wrong_C: 'can to' is ungrammatical; modal 'can' does not take 'to'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'musíte se připojit'. 'Have to' or 'must' expresses technical necessity. Never say *can to*.

questions.prompt: Employees _____ memorize 20 complex passwords if they use the corporate enterprise password manager.

explanations.correct: 'don't have to' expresses lack of necessity (nemusejí si pamatovat).
explanations.wrong_A: 'must not' would mean they are forbidden from memorizing them.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'nemusejí': Absence of obligation is 'don't have to', not *must not* (nesmějí).

questions.prompt: When leaving your workstation, you _____ press Windows + L to lock your screen.

explanations.correct: 'must' emphasizes mandatory compliance with the Clean Desk and Screen Policy.
explanations.wrong_A: 'should' is a gentle recommendation, but screen locking is mandatory in pharma IT.

questions.cz_learning_point: Mandatory security policy requires 'must': 'You must lock your screen'.

questions.prompt: You _____ click on links inside suspicious emails from unknown external senders.

explanations.correct: 'must not' expresses absolute prohibition against clicking phishing links.
explanations.wrong_D: 'don't have to' means it is not required, but permissible if you want.

questions.cz_learning_point: Phishing prevention: 'You must not click...' (nesmíte klikat). Do not use *don't have to*.

questions.prompt: Passphrases _____ contain at least 14 characters, including numbers and symbols.
questions.cz_learning_point: Password policy: 'Passphrases must contain...' (hesla musí obsahovat).

questions.prompt: Visitors _____ be escorted by a badged employee at all times inside the server room.
questions.cz_learning_point: Physical datacenter security: 'Visitors must be escorted' (návštěvy musí být doprovázeny).

questions.prompt: Users _____ disable anti-virus software on their machines under any circumstances.

explanations.wrong_C: 'don't have to' means lack of requirement, not prohibition.

questions.cz_learning_point: Never say *don't have to* for prohibitions. Disabling security tools is strictly 'must not' (nesmějí).
